attributes.name: Logic
attributes.tagline: Two and two, and never a third.
attributes.description: The cold clerk that lives behind your eyes. Logic builds chains of cause and effect and is offended when reality refuses to obey them. It is brilliant at exposing a lie that has the wrong number of moving parts — and useless against a grief that has no parts at all.
attributes.pitfall: At high levels it sneers at people who feel before they think — and misses everything that can't be proven.
attributes.voiceSignature: states the obvious as though it were a verdict

attributes.name: Empathy
attributes.description: The open door. Empathy reads the tremor under a steady voice and knows when a man is lying because the lie costs him something. It will make you weep at a stranger's funeral — and it cannot tell you whether weeping is wise.
attributes.pitfall: It bleeds. Too much Empathy and every con artist's sob story becomes your own debt to repay.
attributes.voiceSignature: speaks softly, from somewhere just behind the sternum

attributes.name: Intuition
attributes.description: The leap across the missing stair. Intuition assembles a conclusion from evidence it never shows you, and is usually — not always — right. It is the part of you that walks into a room and decides, instantly, where the body would be.
attributes.pitfall: Confidence without footnotes. When it's wrong, it is wrong with total conviction.
attributes.voiceSignature: interrupts, certain, before the sentence is finished

attributes.name: Authority
attributes.tagline: They are already obeying. They just don't know it.
attributes.description: The spine. Authority is the part of you that fills a doorway, that turns a question into a command by lowering its voice. It wins the room and loses the friend. Use it on the guilty; never on the grieving.
attributes.pitfall: It mistakes fear for respect, and respect for love. It will make enemies of people you needed.

attributes.name: Creativity
attributes.tagline: What if the wall were a door?
attributes.description: The wild architect. Creativity invents the theory nobody else would dare, finds the third option between two bad ones, and occasionally builds a cathedral of nonsense and insists you live in it. Genius and embarrassment share a birthday.
attributes.pitfall: It would rather be interesting than be right.
attributes.voiceSignature: pitches an idea like it's the best one anyone's ever had

attributes.name: Perception
attributes.tagline: The room is talking. Are you listening?
attributes.description: The thousand small eyes. Perception catches the cigarette burn on the wrong finger, the draught from a door that should be sealed, the name nobody said out loud. It is the difference between a scene and a crime scene.
attributes.pitfall: It floods. Everything is signal; nothing is. The noise can drown the case.
attributes.voiceSignature: names a detail, flatly, and lets it sit there accusing

attributes.name: Composure
attributes.tagline: Let the face hold while the house burns.
attributes.description: The held breath. Composure is the mask you wear so well it becomes a skill — the poker face, the steady hand at the autopsy, the refusal to flinch when a confession lands. It guards your Morale; when it cracks, you crack.
attributes.pitfall: The mask can fuse to the face. People who never flinch sometimes stop feeling.
attributes.voiceSignature: reminds you, quietly, that they are watching your hands

attributes.name: Instinct
attributes.tagline: The body knew the alley was wrong.
attributes.description: The old animal. Instinct is hunger, threat-sense, the prickle on the neck, the readiness to run or to hit first. It keeps the meat alive when the mind is busy being clever. It guards your Endurance; spend it, and the body sends the bill.
attributes.pitfall: It answers every problem with the same two verbs: fight, or flee.
attributes.voiceSignature: speaks in nouns and warnings, never in full sentences
